stories.title: Material selection for aircraft wing spars under uncertainty using Fermatean fuzzy Z-number neutrality aggregation operators
stories.description: There is a need for practical frameworks to assess multiple material characteristics, handle fuzzy expert judgments, and quantify the confidence in those judgments when identifying reliable materials for safety-critical aerospace structures. Most existing aggregation techniques in fuzzy environments do not consider reliability information. While these methods may produce mathematically sound rankings, their practical value remains limited. To fill this gap, this study provides a solid theoretical basis for the neutrality-based aggregation in the Fermatean fuzzy Z-number (FFZN). A novel family of aggregation operators (AO) is introduced, together with novel operational laws, into the environment. Specifically, using weighted averaging, ordered weighted averaging, geometric averaging, ordered weighted geometric, hybrid weighted averaging, and hybrid weighted geometric AOs are built on the FFZN neutrality architecture, aimed at capturing not only the inherent vagueness of expert evaluations but also the confidence level of each assessment. A structured multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) and the criteria-wise aggregation are formulated, followed by the reliability integration. The framework is used for selecting composite materials for aircraft wing spars, which are structures with high requirements in a component that has to meet high loading and performance demands that conflict on many criteria concerning load transfer between the wing and fuselage, such as specific strength, fatigue life, defect rate in manufacturing, and material cost. Four candidate materials that could potentially come together to form a composite material are assessed. By applying the proposed MCDM procedure, the obtained rankings are compared with the well-known methods such as WASPAS, CoCoSo, TOPSIS, and VIKOR. The FFZN neutrality AOs provide more stable and discriminative rankings than existing methods for high-stakes engineering problems, where evaluative vagueness and assessment reliability must be rigorously accounted for.

stories.title: Secure trading of excess solar power in smart buildings using blockchain-enabled RES
stories.description: The use of photovoltaic (PV) systems in smart buildings has greatly promoted renewable energy generation, but efficient use and trading of PV surplus generation are still difficult. This paper introduces a novel energy management framework for transacting surplus solar energy for a secure, decentralized way, among prosumers and grid energy components. It includes smart meters and smart contract implementation, which allow energy to be transacted in real time, in an automatic and transparent way, between two parties in a peer-to-peer (P2P) system. Return on Investment (ROI) ratio is the ratio of net economic benefits achieved by surplus energy trading to the total investment amount of PV infrastructure and implementation of the energy trading blockchain in this study. Is the ROI calculated from the revenue generated from energy sales plus the savings from managing the grid’s electricity portfolio, and add the avoidance of transaction costs CEMS would bear as the lack of intermediaries. The suggested proposal secures data integrity, transparency of transactions, enhanced efficiency and allows optimal use of local energy production. Results show that building owners can improve in their energy management and benefit economically. The study shows that blockchain could be used as an energy trading platform to enable a scalable, reliable solution for decentralized renewable energy (dRE) markets of smart building.

stories.title: A model agnostic procedural framework for reverse concrete mix design using existing artificial intelligence property predictors
stories.description: Artificial intelligence models in concrete materials research usually operate as forward property predictors. They receive mixture variables and curing information, then return an estimated material property. Concrete proportioning, however, normally begins with a required performance condition and proceeds toward a feasible mixture. The gap addressed in this study is the absence of a practical, auditable, model-agnostic protocol for using an existing or fixed forward property predictor within a target-first reverse-design workflow, particularly when the predictor’s development information is incomplete or is not controlled by the end user. This study develops a procedural framework for reverse concrete mix design with existing artificial intelligence property predictors and treats the predictor as a virtual trial evaluator inside a human-guided design procedure. The framework defines stages for target translation, model eligibility screening, candidate feasibility, reverse trial adjustment, uncertainty-aware acceptance, engineering coherence checking, and reproducible reporting. A numerical case study using a 3544-record concrete mixture dataset trained an extremely randomized trees predictor and applied the proposed gates to a 40 MPa, 28-day reverse design target. The predictor achieved test R2 = 0.972, RMSE = 6.63 MPa, and MAE = 4.18 MPa; the calibration-based uncertainty allowance was 8.25 MPa. Using the conservative score, 42 of 149 held-out feasible candidates were accepted, and 40 of those accepted candidates had measured strength not less than 40 MPa. The selected minimum-binder candidate had predicted strength 51.68 MPa and measured strength 49.30 MPa. The contribution is procedural and validation-focused rather than a new optimization algorithm, and the final AI-assisted candidate remains subject to laboratory and specification verification.

stories.title: The effects of physical emotion intensity and perceived emotions on trait and ability judgments are non-linear
stories.description: Facial expressions are important cues for trait inferences, yet most research focuses on intense, prototypical displays, leaving open how observers interpret ambiguous or blended expressions. Across two studies, we examined how anger–sadness morphs shape emotion perception and social judgments, and whether these effects differ by expresser gender. Study 1 revealed categorical perception of anger–sadness blends, with male faces categorized as angry at lower physical anger intensities than female faces. Study 2 showed that female faces were perceived as sadder and male faces as angrier primarily at lower physical anger intensities. Social judgments varied non-linearly with perceived anger and sadness, with the pattern differing by judgment domain and expresser gender. Higher perceived anger predicted greater dominance, lower affiliation, and, for male expressers, greater leadership ability, whereas higher perceived sadness predicted lower dominance and leadership ability. Crucially, gender differences in social judgments were reduced once perceived anger and sadness were taken into account. Thus, anger–sadness morphs reveal socially structured, non-linear patterns of emotion perception and person judgment that may be missed by focusing only on prototypical endpoint expressions.

stories.title: Reconfigurable multibeam engineering of Marangoni convection for programmable optofluidic steering
stories.description: Optofluidic manipulation provides a powerful route for guiding micro- and nanoparticles, yet conventional light-induced flow systems often suffer from limited controllability, unstable flow patterns, and poor reconfigurability. Here, we demonstrate programmable optofluidic steering based on multibeam engineering of Marangoni convection technique (MEMCT) around optothermally generated air bubbles. In our MEMCT, focused laser irradiation on a gold film creates localized photothermal heating near an air bubble, thereby reshaping the temperature distribution along the air–water interface. By varying the position, number, and spatial arrangement of laser-induced heat sources, we generate tunable flow patterns ranging from directional transport to complex vortical circulation. Simulations and experiments confirm that these reconfigurable interfacial stress fields can deterministically steer single or multiple particles along prescribed trajectories. Furthermore, by integrating it with microfluidic cross-junctions and extending this strategy to bubble arrays, we realize pump-free, on-demand particle routing. This programmable Marangoni-flow platform offers a simple and versatile strategy for dynamic particle manipulation, with potential applications in lab-on-a-chip systems, micro/nanorobotics, and biophotonic technologies. Optofluidic manipulation primarily relied on fixed geometries and optical forces, which limited the controllability and reconfigurability of flow patterns for particle steering. Here, the authors achieved a programmable, pump-free optofluidic platform enabling precise, on-demand manipulation and directional routing of microparticles and biological cells with sub-micrometer accuracy.

stories.title: Tracking twolined spittlebug, Prosapia bicincta, movement in upland pastures of Hawaiʻi
stories.description: The twolined spittlebug, Prosapia bicincta (TLSB), is an invasive pasture pest on Hawaiʻi Island and causes extensive damage to rangelands. Despite a rapid spread, field-based estimates of adult TLSB movement remain limited. Here, we evaluate the feasibility of harmonic radar (HR) tracking to quantify short-term movement of adult TLSB in two upcountry pastures on Hawaiʻi Island. HR-tagged adults were released at two sites and tracked over ~ 24 h, achieving 95% recovery and observing a mean displacement of ~ 0.6 m (Experiment 1). Induced movements of tagged and untagged adults were recorded to assess potential tag effects; no statistical difference in movement distance was detected between treatments but the observed probability of movement behaviors (jump vs. jump-flight) differed (Experiment 2). However, testing and environmental variability suggest this result should be interpreted cautiously. While tag effects on survival and behavior are not fully characterized, our results provide evidence consistent with limited short-term impacts under field conditions. Males moved farther than females in both experiments. Correlated random walk simulations based on observed movement parameters estimated that 95% of lifetime movements occur within ~ 8 m of the origin under the conditions tested. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of HR tracking for TLSB and provide baseline data to inform future studies on dispersal and management.

stories.title: Level III neonatal intensive care unit heterogeneity in patients, services, and outcomes
stories.description: Level III NICUs share one AAP level of care designation. We characterized variation, identified sub-classes, and compared sub-class outcomes. This retrospective cohort analysis of level III NICUs in Florida, Michigan, Oregon, Pennsylvania, and South Carolina used linked hospital discharge-vital statistics data (2010–2020). Included hospitals had ≥10 births annually and infants had gestational age <32 weeks and/or birth weight <1500 g. We characterized NICU-level heterogeneity; used latent class analysis (LCA) to obtain sub-classes; and compared risk-adjusted outcomes with multivariable Poisson regression. Among 163 NICUs (1518 hospital-years) there was significant variation. LCA identified five sub-classes (3a–e). Preterm volume and procedural intensity rose with acuity (3a lowest, 3d/3e highest). Higher acuity was associated with lower mortality but higher morbidity (3d vs. 3a: death: IRR 0.59 [95% CI 0.54–0.65]; morbidity: 2.84 [2.43–3.31]). Level III NICUs are heterogeneous and comprise five sub-classes with divergent outcomes. Sub-classification may facilitate risk-appropriate care.
